framework.name: FastAPI
framework.tagline: Modern, type-hint-driven Python APIs with automatic docs.
framework.overview: FastAPI turns Python type hints into request parsing, validation (via Pydantic), and OpenAPI docs. Master it by defining path operations, typed params, validated request bodies, dependency injection, async endpoints with status codes, and clean error handling.

challenges.title: 1. First path operation
challenges.concept: A path operation is a function decorated with `@app.get("/path")`. Whatever it returns is serialized to JSON automatically.

challenges.title: 2. Typed path and query params
challenges.concept: Type-annotated function args become validated inputs: a `{id}` in the path is a path param, extra args are query params with defaults.
challenges.goal: GET /users/{id}?verbose=false returns the parsed values, coercing types.
steps: Annotate id: int and verbose: bool = False.
hints: Args not in the path become query params.

challenges.title: 3. Validate a request body
challenges.concept: A Pydantic `BaseModel` typed as a parameter is parsed from the JSON body and validated. Constraint types like `EmailStr` enforce format.
challenges.goal: POST /users validates {name, email} and echoes the model.
steps: Define CreateUser(BaseModel) with name: str, email: EmailStr.
Add a min length on name with Field.
Accept it as a typed parameter and return it.
challenges.starterCode:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel, EmailStr, Field

app = FastAPI()

class CreateUser(BaseModel):
    # TODO
    pass

challenges.title: 4. Dependency injection
challenges.concept: `Depends` wires reusable logic (auth, pagination, db sessions) into handlers. FastAPI resolves and injects the dependency's return value.
challenges.goal: Inject pagination params via a dependency into GET /items.
steps: Add a handler param params: dict = Depends(pagination).
hints: Depends(callable) runs the callable per request.
Dependencies can have their own query params.

challenges.title: 5. Async endpoint with status code
challenges.concept: Use `async def` for IO-bound handlers so the event loop can serve other requests while awaiting. Set `status_code` on the decorator for creation semantics.
challenges.goal: POST /notes returns 201 from an async handler.
steps: await a coroutine (simulate IO) then return the created note.
hints: await asyncio.sleep(0) stands in for real IO.
challenges.starterCode:
import asyncio
from fastapi import FastAPI, status
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()

class Note(BaseModel):
    text: str

# TODO: async POST /notes returning 201
challenges.solution:
import asyncio
from fastapi import FastAPI, status
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()

class Note(BaseModel):
    text: str

@app.post("/notes", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def create_note(note: Note):
    await asyncio.sleep(0)
    return note

challenges.title: 6. Error handling
challenges.concept: Raise `HTTPException` for expected errors, or register an `@app.exception_handler` to map a custom exception to a consistent JSON response app-wide.
challenges.goal: GET /users/{id} raises 404 for unknown ids via a custom handler.
steps: Define a NotFound(Exception) carrying a message.
Raise NotFound from the handler when the id is missing.
